title: Phong Nha–Ke Bang National Park
summary: Phong Nha–Ke Bang is a limestone karst landscape on the Viet Nam–Laos border, with caves and underground rivers whose formation began about 400 million years ago. Viet Nam's Prime Minister upgraded the nature reserve to a national park in December 2001, and UNESCO inscribed the property in 2003.

uncertainty.note: Start is the December 2001 upgrade to national park (IUCN evaluation); end of range is the 2003 World Heritage inscription (UNESCO). The karst itself is far older.

where.modern_name: Phong Nha–Ke Bang National Park, Viet Nam (transboundary with Hin Nam No, Laos)
where.historical_name: Phong Nha–Ke Bang National Park, Socialist Republic of Viet Nam

importance.justification: World Heritage karst landscape of Asia's oldest large-scale karst system, with globally significant caves.
